Compute the edge betweenness of a network

Source: R/centrality.R
net_edge_betweenness.Rd

net_edge_betweenness() computes the betweenness of each edge in a network. Edge betweenness describes the role of an edge in connecting the network: it counts how many of the shortest paths between pairs of nodes run through the edge. An edge with high betweenness links parts of the network that would otherwise be far apart, for example two groups of closely related symptoms.

The function finds shortest paths on the absolute edge weights, inverted to distances so that a strong association is a short step (with invert = FALSE the weights are used as distances). When two nodes are joined by several equally short paths, each path counts as its share, 1 / (number of such paths).

It returns one row per edge. The value is a count, as returned by igraph::edge_betweenness(), not a proportion: on the path a-b-c-d-e the four edges score 4, 6, 6 and 4.

For the betweenness of nodes, use net_centralities(); for the connections of nodes to predefined communities, use net_bridge().

Usage

net_edge_betweenness(x, invert = TRUE, labels = NULL)

Arguments

x

A fitted network (psychnet) or a square weighted adjacency matrix. A bare matrix that is not symmetric is treated as directed, the entry in row i and column j being the edge from node i to node j.

invert

If TRUE (default), edge weights are inverted to distances (strong association = short path); if FALSE, weights are distances.

labels

Optional node labels for a bare matrix, one unique label per node.

Value

A data frame with one row per edge and columns from, to and edge_betweenness (the number of shortest paths through the edge). An undirected network has one row per edge, counting each pair of nodes once; a directed network has one row per arc, counting ordered pairs.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when x is not a fitted network or a square numeric matrix, contains non-finite weights, or labels does not give one unique label per node.

See also

net_centralities() for node betweenness and other measures; net_bridge() for bridge centrality.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:6, 1:6, "-"))
net_edge_betweenness(ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 400))
#>   from to edge_betweenness
#> 1   V1 V2                5
#> 2   V2 V3                8
#> 3   V3 V4                9
#> 4   V4 V5                8
#> 5   V5 V6                5
